---
title: "Raster Gap Filler"
date: 2026-09-20
categories: [tool, geostatistics]
description: "Upload a multi-band raster and fill the gaps in one band using a second, fully-populated band as a covariate — cokriging instead of single-variable kriging. Runs entirely in your browser, powered by R."
page-layout: full
---

Upload a raster with two or more bands — a satellite band with cloud
gaps, a field survey rasterized with mostly-empty cells, anything with
real holes in it — pick the band to fill (the *target*) and, if you
have one, a second band with no gaps that's correlated with it (the
*covariate*, elevation or another spectral band are common choices).
This tool fits a variogram model between the two, then predicts the
target's missing values from wherever the covariate is available —
cokriging, not just averaging nearby pixels. Skip the covariate and it
falls back to ordinary kriging on the target band's own known pixels.

::: {.callout-tip}
**Private by design.** Your file is processed entirely in your browser
(R via WebAssembly) — it's never uploaded to any server, including
ours. Nothing to configure, nothing to trust: the code never gets the
chance to see your data.
:::

```{.webgeods-r #raster-gap-filler-example-r}
#| package: terra
library(terra)

# Two bands, deliberately with two DIFFERENT gaps, not "one gap in the
# target, nothing missing in the covariate" -- the covariate having a
# gap of its own (a shorter revisit on one satellite band, a different
# cloud mask, anything a real multi-band product commonly has) is the
# case this tool actually needs to handle correctly, not a corner case
# to gloss over in its own example.
set.seed(42)
n <- 25
xs <- 0:(n - 1)
ys <- 0:(n - 1)

# Same Gaussian-hill shape reused across this project's raster examples
# (raster-inspector.qmd, viewshed-calculator.qmd) -- a reader who's
# already seen one recognizes it here too. The covariate is a scaled,
# shifted, independently-noised version of the SAME underlying trend,
# not a copy of the target -- real enough correlation for cokriging to
# find, not a giveaway.
trend <- outer(ys, xs, function(y, x) 100 + 40 * exp(-((x - 12)^2 + (y - 12)^2) / 40))

target <- trend + matrix(rnorm(n * n, sd = 1.5), nrow = n)
covariate <- 0.6 * trend + 20 + matrix(rnorm(n * n, sd = 2), nrow = n)

# The target's own gap: one contiguous block (rows/cols 8-16), the
# shape a real gap-filling problem actually looks like -- not pixels
# scattered at random, which would be a much easier, unrealistic case.
target[9:17, 9:17] <- NA

# The covariate's own gap: smaller, and only PARTLY inside the
# target's -- rows/cols 12-14 sit inside the target's 9-17 block, but
# most of the target's gap still has the covariate available. This
# gives the example three real regions at once: covariate available
# where the target isn't (cokriging's actual job), both missing at
# once (nothing to predict from, stays empty), and both present
# (where the model gets fit).
covariate[12:14, 12:14] <- NA

band_target <- rast(target, crs = "EPSG:4326")
band_covariate <- rast(covariate, crs = "EPSG:4326")
ext(band_target) <- c(12.40, 12.40 + n * 0.004, 41.90, 41.90 + n * 0.004)
ext(band_covariate) <- ext(band_target)
names(band_target) <- "target"
names(band_covariate) <- "covariate"

r <- c(band_target, band_covariate)
writeRaster(r, "/uploaded.tif", overwrite = TRUE, filetype = "GTiff")

"example 2-band raster written"
```

```{.webgeods-r #raster-gap-filler-inspect-r}
#| package: terra, jsonlite
library(terra)

path <- NULL
for (candidate in c("/uploaded.tif")) {
  ok <- tryCatch({ rast(candidate); TRUE }, error = function(e) FALSE)
  if (ok) { path <- candidate; break }
}

summary_out <- NULL
footprint <- list(type = jsonlite::unbox("FeatureCollection"), features = list())
bands_out <- list()

if (!is.null(path)) {
  r <- rast(path)

  # Per-band valid/NA counts -- the whole reason this needs its own
  # pass before the reader picks anything: a band with a lot of NA is
  # a plausible target, a band with none is a plausible covariate, and
  # neither is obvious from band count/names alone.
  band_stats <- lapply(seq_len(nlyr(r)), function(i) {
    band <- r[[i]]
    n_total <- ncell(band)
    n_na <- as.numeric(global(is.na(band), "sum")[1, 1])
    list(
      band = jsonlite::unbox(i),
      name = jsonlite::unbox(names(r)[i]),
      naCount = jsonlite::unbox(n_na),
      naFraction = jsonlite::unbox(round(n_na / n_total, 4))
    )
  })

  # Suggested target: the band with the most NA (ties broken by lower
  # index) -- a default, not a lock, the reader can always pick a
  # different pair.
  na_fractions <- sapply(band_stats, function(b) b$naFraction)
  suggested_target <- if (any(na_fractions > 0)) which.max(na_fractions) else 1

  # as.vector(ext(r)) keeps its own names (xmin/xmax/ymin/ymax) --
  # jsonlite serializes a NAMED numeric as a JSON object ({"xmin":
  # 12.4}), not a plain number, so each coordinate needs an explicit
  # as.numeric() (unname() alone isn't enough once it's inside a
  # list()) before it can sit inside a GeoJSON coordinate pair.
  bnds <- as.vector(ext(r))
  xmin <- as.numeric(bnds["xmin"]); xmax <- as.numeric(bnds["xmax"])
  ymin <- as.numeric(bnds["ymin"]); ymax <- as.numeric(bnds["ymax"])
  footprint <- list(
    type = jsonlite::unbox("FeatureCollection"),
    features = list(list(
      type = jsonlite::unbox("Feature"),
      properties = list(name = jsonlite::unbox("raster footprint")),
      geometry = list(
        type = jsonlite::unbox("Polygon"),
        coordinates = list(list(
          list(xmin, ymin), list(xmax, ymin),
          list(xmax, ymax), list(xmin, ymax),
          list(xmin, ymin)
        ))
      )
    ))
  )

  # Same reprojection this cell's own compute/export siblings already
  # need (a bare SpatExtent can't go through project() directly; see
  # their own comment for why) -- the live target/covariate preview
  # below needs it too, to place the raster correctly for a file whose
  # native CRS isn't already WGS84.
  to_minx_miny_maxx_maxy <- function(spat_extent) {
    b <- as.vector(spat_extent)
    c(as.numeric(b["xmin"]), as.numeric(b["ymin"]), as.numeric(b["xmax"]), as.numeric(b["ymax"]))
  }
  wgs84_bounds <- tryCatch({
    poly_wgs84 <- project(as.polygons(ext(r), crs = crs(r)), "EPSG:4326")
    to_minx_miny_maxx_maxy(ext(poly_wgs84))
  }, error = function(e) to_minx_miny_maxx_maxy(ext(r)))

  # Every band's own raw values, base64-encoded the same way the
  # compute cell encodes its filled result -- lets the map preview the
  # target/covariate bands the reader currently has picked WITHOUT a
  # round trip through R each time they change a dropdown (cokriging
  # itself only runs once Fill is actually pressed).
  bands_out <- lapply(seq_len(nlyr(r)), function(i) {
    vals <- as.numeric(values(r[[i]]))
    valid <- vals[!is.na(vals)]
    con <- rawConnection(raw(0), "wb")
    writeBin(vals, con, size = 4, endian = "little")
    raw_bytes <- rawConnectionValue(con)
    close(con)
    list(
      band = jsonlite::unbox(i),
      data = jsonlite::unbox(jsonlite::base64_enc(raw_bytes)),
      min = if (length(valid) > 0) jsonlite::unbox(min(valid)) else NULL,
      max = if (length(valid) > 0) jsonlite::unbox(max(valid)) else NULL
    )
  })

  summary_out <- list(
    width = jsonlite::unbox(ncol(r)),
    height = jsonlite::unbox(nrow(r)),
    bandCount = jsonlite::unbox(nlyr(r)),
    crs = jsonlite::unbox(crs(r, describe = TRUE)$name),
    bandStats = band_stats,
    suggestedTarget = jsonlite::unbox(suggested_target),
    wgs84Bounds = round(wgs84_bounds, 6)
  )
}

list(summary = summary_out, footprint = footprint, bands = bands_out)
```

The code itself isn't shown here — it's a fixed, non-editable
computation using `gstat`'s cokriging (linear model of
coregionalization) underneath. Want to see the same pipeline built up
one step at a time, why a covariate band helps, and why this runs on
R, not Python? Read
[Filling Raster Gaps with Cokriging](/posts/cokriging-raster-gap-filling.html).

```{.webgeods-r #raster-gap-filler-compute-r}
#| inject: [targetBand, covariateBand, variogramModel, nmax]
#| package: sf, sp, gstat, terra, jsonlite
library(sf)
library(sp)
library(gstat)
library(terra)

target_i <- as.integer(targetBand)
covariate_i <- if (identical(covariateBand, "None")) NA_integer_ else as.integer(covariateBand)

if (!is.na(covariate_i) && covariate_i == target_i) {
  stop("Target and covariate must be different bands — pick two distinct bands, or set the covariate to \"None\".")
}

r <- rast("/uploaded.tif")

# The terra -> sp bridge: gstat's own variogram()/krige()/fit.lmc()
# take sp point objects (coordinates(df) <- ~x+y), not a terra
# SpatRaster or SpatVector -- terra doesn't provide that replacement
# function itself. crds()/values() give cell centers and per-band
# values aligned by row, in the file's OWN crs (no reprojection here,
# unlike kriging-interpolator.qmd's point-survey case: a raster's
# pixels already sit on a grid with a real resolution, not raw lon/lat
# survey coordinates that need a working CRS to make distance
# meaningful).
cell_xy <- crds(r, na.rm = FALSE)
target_vals <- as.numeric(values(r[[target_i]]))
df <- data.frame(x = cell_xy[, 1], y = cell_xy[, 2], target = target_vals)

has_covariate <- !is.na(covariate_i)
if (has_covariate) {
  df$covariate <- as.numeric(values(r[[covariate_i]]))
}

fit_method_used <- NA_integer_

if (!has_covariate) {

  # No covariate: ordinary kriging on the target band's own known
  # pixels, same shape as kriging-interpolator-compute-r's own
  # variogram()/fit.variogram()/krige() sequence, just with the raster's
  # OWN valid cells standing in for uploaded sample points.
  fit_df <- df[!is.na(df$target), ]
  pred_df <- df[is.na(df$target), ]

  if (nrow(fit_df) < 5) {
    stop(paste0("Need at least 5 valid pixels in the target band to fit a variogram — found ", nrow(fit_df), "."))
  }

  fit_pts <- fit_df
  coordinates(fit_pts) <- ~x + y

  v_emp <- variogram(target ~ 1, fit_pts)
  init_range <- max(v_emp$dist) / 3
  init_psill <- var(fit_df$target)
  v_model <- tryCatch(
    fit.variogram(v_emp, vgm(psill = init_psill, model = variogramModel, range = init_range, nugget = init_psill / 4)),
    error = function(e) NULL
  )
  if (is.null(v_model) || isTRUE(attr(v_model, "singular")) || any(v_model$psill < 0)) {
    stop(paste0("Could not fit a ", variogramModel, " variogram model to this band's known pixels."))
  }

  cv <- tryCatch(gstat.cv(gstat(id = "target", formula = target ~ 1, data = fit_pts, model = v_model), nfold = 5, verbose = FALSE), error = function(e) NULL)
  rmse <- if (!is.null(cv)) sqrt(mean(cv$residual^2, na.rm = TRUE)) else NA

  filled <- df$target

  if (nrow(pred_df) > 0) {
    pred_pts <- pred_df
    coordinates(pred_pts) <- ~x + y
    k <- krige(target ~ 1, fit_pts, pred_pts, model = v_model, nmax = as.numeric(nmax), debug.level = 0)
    filled[is.na(df$target)] <- as.numeric(k$var1.pred)
  }

  # Same three numbers kriging-interpolator.qmd's own stats card
  # reports, plus the fitting sample's own mean/variance -- nugget +
  # partial sill landing far from that variance is the easiest sign a
  # fit went wrong, without this tool asserting a pass/fail verdict
  # itself (a fixed threshold would flag genuinely non-stationary data
  # as "bad" just as often as an actual bad fit).
  nugget_val <- v_model$psill[1]
  partial_sill_val <- v_model$psill[2]
  range_val <- v_model$range[2]
  sample_mean <- mean(fit_df$target)
  sample_variance <- var(fit_df$target)

  v_line <- variogramLine(v_model, maxdist = max(v_emp$dist), n = 100)
  variogram_out <- list(
    target = list(
      nugget = jsonlite::unbox(round(nugget_val, 4)),
      partialSill = jsonlite::unbox(round(partial_sill_val, 4)),
      # dist rounded to 6dp, not 3 -- this raster's own coordinates are
      # degree-scale (a range around 0.01-0.05), so 3dp was coarse
      # enough to round SEVERAL of variogramLine()'s 100 points to the
      # identical x value while their y still rose smoothly between
      # them -- found live: a fitted "curve" that was actually a
      # staircase, each repeated x plotted as a vertical jump followed
      # by a flat run to the next one.
      empirical = list(dist = round(v_emp$dist, 6), gamma = round(v_emp$gamma, 5), npairs = v_emp$np),
      fitted = list(dist = round(v_line$dist, 6), gamma = round(v_line$gamma, 5))
    )
  )

} else {

  # data_fit: pixels where BOTH bands are valid -- fitting only, never
  # prediction. data_pred: pixels where the COVARIATE is valid,
  # regardless of the target -- this must include data_fit's own
  # locations too (it does automatically, since data_fit is already a
  # subset of "covariate valid"). Do NOT narrow data_pred to just the
  # target's own gaps -- gstat needs the already-known target pixels
  # present in data_pred for the cokriging system's local context, or
  # it silently breaks.
  data_fit <- df[!is.na(df$target) & !is.na(df$covariate), ]
  data_pred <- df[!is.na(df$covariate), ]

  if (nrow(data_fit) < 5) {
    stop(paste0("Need at least 5 pixels where both the target and covariate bands are valid to fit a coregionalization model — found ", nrow(data_fit), "."))
  }

  fit_pts <- data_fit
  coordinates(fit_pts) <- ~x + y

  v_emp <- variogram(target ~ 1, fit_pts)
  init_psill <- var(data_fit$target)

  # Both variables registered on the SAME point object (fit_pts, same
  # rows, same order) -- registering them on mismatched location sets
  # instead forces gstat to compute a genuine zero-distance bin between
  # the two variables' own locations, which fit.method=7 (Cressie's
  # weights, gstat's own default) divides by.
  v_cross <- variogram(gstat(gstat(NULL, id = "target", formula = target ~ 1, data = fit_pts), id = "covariate", formula = covariate ~ 1, data = fit_pts))

  # fit.lmc()'s own optimizer is local, not global -- the single
  # init_range = max(dist)/3 guess this used to pass it (a reasonable
  # rule of thumb for an ordinary single-variable fit.variogram())
  # routinely trapped the JOINT fit in a much worse local optimum here:
  # confirmed live, trying several starting ranges on the same data,
  # sum-of-squared-error against the target's own empirical points
  # ranged from 1878 (at max/3) down to 173 (at the full max distance)
  # -- a ~10x difference, with the target's fitted sill/range moving
  # enough to visibly matter on the chart, not just in the decimals.
  # Trying a small spread of starting points and keeping whichever
  # converges closest to the target's own empirical variogram is the
  # robust fix: no single fixed fraction is a good guess for every
  # raster a reader uploads, but "try several, keep the best" doesn't
  # need to guess right the first time.
  sse_against_target <- function(model_df) {
    vl <- variogramLine(model_df, dist_vector = v_emp$dist)
    sum((v_emp$gamma - vl$gamma)^2)
  }
  fit_lmc_candidate <- function(init_range) {
    lmc_model <- vgm(psill = init_psill, model = variogramModel, range = init_range, nugget = init_psill / 4)
    fresh_g <- function() gstat(gstat(NULL, id = "target", formula = target ~ 1, data = fit_pts), id = "covariate", formula = covariate ~ 1, data = fit_pts)
    gf <- tryCatch(fit.lmc(v_cross, fresh_g(), model = lmc_model, fit.method = 7, correct.diagonal = 1.01), error = function(e) NULL)
    method <- 7
    if (is.null(gf)) {
      gf <- tryCatch(fit.lmc(v_cross, fresh_g(), model = lmc_model, fit.method = 1, correct.diagonal = 1.01), error = function(e) NULL)
      method <- 1
    }
    if (is.null(gf)) return(NULL)
    list(g_fit = gf, method = method, sse = sse_against_target(gf$model[["target"]]))
  }

  candidates <- Filter(Negate(is.null), lapply(max(v_cross$dist) * c(1 / 6, 1 / 3, 2 / 3, 1), fit_lmc_candidate))
  if (length(candidates) == 0) {
    stop(paste0("Could not fit a coregionalization model between these two bands (often too few co-located pixels, or the bands aren't actually correlated)."))
  }
  best <- candidates[[which.min(sapply(candidates, function(c) c$sse))]]
  g_fit <- best$g_fit
  fit_method_used <- best$method

  # gstat.cv() on a multivariate (cokriging) gstat object names its
  # result columns "target.pred"/"target.var" (id-prefixed, since more
  # than one variable is registered) but the residual/observed/zscore
  # columns are NOT prefixed -- just "residual", found empirically
  # (cv$target.residual doesn't exist and silently produced NaN/null
  # instead of erroring, since `$` on a missing data.frame column
  # returns NULL rather than raising).
  cv <- tryCatch(gstat.cv(g_fit, nfold = 5, verbose = FALSE), error = function(e) NULL)
  rmse <- if (!is.null(cv)) sqrt(mean(cv$residual^2, na.rm = TRUE)) else NA

  pred_pts <- data_pred
  coordinates(pred_pts) <- ~x + y

  # Target on its own known locations (fit_pts), covariate on ALL of
  # data_pred -- then attach the already-fitted model as a SEPARATE
  # step. Passing model= directly into this gstat() call throws
  # "argument 'formula' is missing" (it reads it as a brand-new
  # variable, not the existing fit); this plain assignment after the
  # fact is the version that actually works.
  g_pred <- gstat(NULL, id = "target", formula = target ~ 1, data = fit_pts)
  g_pred <- gstat(g_pred, id = "covariate", formula = covariate ~ 1, data = pred_pts)
  g_pred$model <- g_fit$model

  k <- predict(g_pred, newdata = pred_pts, nmax = as.numeric(nmax), debug.level = 0)

  filled <- df$target
  pred_index <- which(!is.na(df$covariate))
  cokriged <- is.na(df$target[pred_index])
  filled[pred_index[cokriged]] <- as.numeric(k$target.pred[cokriged])

  # Pixels the covariate itself couldn't reach: target NA, covariate
  # also NA. Left as NA on purpose -- no fallback pass to plain kriging
  # here, see raster-gap-filler.qmd's own closing note for why (the
  # reader can rerun this tool a second time on the result, with no
  # covariate, if they want those filled too).

  # Stats card numbers: the TARGET's own component of the joint fit --
  # fit.lmc() names the three pieces of an LMC "target", "covariate"
  # and "target.covariate" (the cross term), each a normal 2-row vgm
  # model (Nug + the chosen shape), confirmed live rather than assumed
  # from the docs. Reporting target's own nugget/sill/range here keeps
  # this row meaning the same thing it means in the no-covariate
  # branch above -- the target band's own spatial structure -- even
  # though the fit that produced it also used the covariate.
  target_model <- g_fit$model[["target"]]
  covariate_model <- g_fit$model[["covariate"]]
  cross_model <- g_fit$model[["target.covariate"]]

  nugget_val <- target_model$psill[1]
  partial_sill_val <- target_model$psill[2]
  range_val <- target_model$range[2]
  sample_mean <- mean(data_fit$target)
  sample_variance <- var(data_fit$target)

  # All three curves for the side panel's charts -- v_cross already
  # holds target's, covariate's AND the cross term's empirical points
  # in one data.frame (an `id` column, not three separate calls), and
  # variogramLine() accepts each piece of g_fit$model exactly like a
  # plain fit.variogram() result. Nothing here is a new computation:
  # fit.lmc() above already produced all of it, just never read back
  # out until now. Each series carries its OWN nugget/partialSill (the
  # shared range lives once in summary$range, since fit.lmc() gives
  # every component the same range by construction) so the side panel
  # can draw a correctly-labeled reference line on all three, not just
  # the one summary already covers.
  max_dist <- max(v_cross$dist)
  # 6dp, not 3 -- same fix as the no-covariate branch above, for the
  # same reason (this raster's degree-scale coordinates need finer
  # rounding than a meter-scale one would, or variogramLine()'s 100
  # points collapse onto a handful of duplicate x values and the
  # "curve" plots as a staircase instead).
  fitted_line <- function(model_df) {
    vl <- variogramLine(model_df, maxdist = max_dist, n = 100)
    list(dist = round(vl$dist, 6), gamma = round(vl$gamma, 5))
  }
  empirical_for <- function(id_name) {
    sub <- v_cross[v_cross$id == id_name, ]
    list(dist = round(sub$dist, 6), gamma = round(sub$gamma, 5), npairs = sub$np)
  }
  variogram_out <- list(
    target = list(
      nugget = jsonlite::unbox(round(nugget_val, 4)),
      partialSill = jsonlite::unbox(round(partial_sill_val, 4)),
      empirical = empirical_for("target"), fitted = fitted_line(target_model)
    ),
    covariate = list(
      nugget = jsonlite::unbox(round(covariate_model$psill[1], 4)),
      partialSill = jsonlite::unbox(round(covariate_model$psill[2], 4)),
      empirical = empirical_for("covariate"), fitted = fitted_line(covariate_model)
    ),
    cross = list(
      nugget = jsonlite::unbox(round(cross_model$psill[1], 4)),
      partialSill = jsonlite::unbox(round(cross_model$psill[2], 4)),
      empirical = empirical_for("target.covariate"), fitted = fitted_line(cross_model)
    )
  )

}

# One definition covers both branches -- any pixel that went from NA
# to a real value, regardless of which branch (or which method inside
# it) put it there. A per-branch count here was the actual bug: the
# no-covariate branch is ordinary kriging, not "filled from
# covariate", so a field literally named that read 0 there even though
# every reachable gap really had just been filled.
n_filled <- sum(!is.na(filled)) - sum(!is.na(df$target))

n_still_na <- sum(is.na(filled))

filled_band <- rast(matrix(filled, nrow = nrow(r), ncol = ncol(r), byrow = TRUE), extent = ext(r), crs = crs(r))
names(filled_band) <- names(r)[target_i]

valid_filled <- filled[!is.na(filled)]

# terra::project() doesn't take a bare SpatExtent -- the documented,
# correct way to reproject just a bounding box is to wrap it as a
# SpatVector polygon first (as.polygons()), project THAT, then read
# its extent back. round()/as.vector() on the extent's own named
# xmin/xmax/ymin/ymax would keep those names, and jsonlite serializes
# a NAMED vector as a JSON OBJECT ({"xmin": ...}) instead of a plain
# array -- setRasterImage() (shared/map-raster.js) destructures
# `bounds` positionally ([minx, miny, maxx, maxy] = bounds), which
# throws "bounds is not iterable" on a plain object, not a graceful
# failure. Each coordinate goes through an explicit as.numeric() to
# strip its name before assembly, same fix as the footprint above.
to_minx_miny_maxx_maxy <- function(spat_extent) {
  b <- as.vector(spat_extent)  # named xmin/xmax/ymin/ymax, terra's own order
  c(as.numeric(b["xmin"]), as.numeric(b["ymin"]), as.numeric(b["xmax"]), as.numeric(b["ymax"]))
}
wgs84_bounds <- tryCatch({
  poly_wgs84 <- project(as.polygons(ext(r), crs = crs(r)), "EPSG:4326")
  to_minx_miny_maxx_maxy(ext(poly_wgs84))
}, error = function(e) to_minx_miny_maxx_maxy(ext(r)))

con <- rawConnection(raw(0), "wb")
writeBin(as.numeric(filled), con, size = 4, endian = "little")
raw_bytes <- rawConnectionValue(con)
close(con)
filled_b64 <- jsonlite::base64_enc(raw_bytes)

list(
  summary = list(
    targetBand = jsonlite::unbox(target_i),
    covariateBand = if (has_covariate) jsonlite::unbox(covariate_i) else NULL,
    variogramModel = jsonlite::unbox(variogramModel),
    nmax = jsonlite::unbox(as.numeric(nmax)),
    pixelsFilled = jsonlite::unbox(n_filled),
    pixelsStillEmpty = jsonlite::unbox(n_still_na),
    crossValidationRmse = if (is.na(rmse)) NULL else jsonlite::unbox(round(rmse, 4)),
    nugget = jsonlite::unbox(round(nugget_val, 4)),
    partialSill = jsonlite::unbox(round(partial_sill_val, 4)),
    range = jsonlite::unbox(round(range_val, 3)),
    sampleMean = jsonlite::unbox(round(sample_mean, 4)),
    sampleVariance = jsonlite::unbox(round(sample_variance, 4)),
    # Only surfaced when the Cressie-weighted fit (fit.method=7,
    # gstat's own default -- tried first, fits noticeably better) had
    # to fall back to the cruder N-only weighting -- the expected path
    # stays silent, same "only mention the exceptional state" pattern
    # "Still empty" below already uses.
    fitMethodFallback = if (has_covariate && fit_method_used == 1) jsonlite::unbox(TRUE) else NULL
  ),
  raster = list(
    width = jsonlite::unbox(ncol(r)),
    height = jsonlite::unbox(nrow(r)),
    data = jsonlite::unbox(filled_b64),
    wgs84Bounds = round(wgs84_bounds, 6),
    min = jsonlite::unbox(round(min(valid_filled), 4)),
    max = jsonlite::unbox(round(max(valid_filled), 4))
  ),
  variogram = variogram_out
)
```

```{.webgeods-r #raster-gap-filler-export-r}
#| inject: [targetBand, covariateBand, variogramModel, nmax]
#| package: sf, sp, gstat, terra, jsonlite
# Recomputes the same pipeline (cheap relative to re-reading the
# source file) and writes the filled target band as an actual GeoTIFF
# via terra::writeRaster() -- same structure as
# kriging-interpolator-export-r.
library(sf)
library(sp)
library(gstat)
library(terra)

target_i <- as.integer(targetBand)
covariate_i <- if (identical(covariateBand, "None")) NA_integer_ else as.integer(covariateBand)

r <- rast("/uploaded.tif")
cell_xy <- crds(r, na.rm = FALSE)
target_vals <- as.numeric(values(r[[target_i]]))
df <- data.frame(x = cell_xy[, 1], y = cell_xy[, 2], target = target_vals)

has_covariate <- !is.na(covariate_i)
if (has_covariate) df$covariate <- as.numeric(values(r[[covariate_i]]))

if (!has_covariate) {

  fit_df <- df[!is.na(df$target), ]
  pred_df <- df[is.na(df$target), ]
  fit_pts <- fit_df
  coordinates(fit_pts) <- ~x + y
  v_emp <- variogram(target ~ 1, fit_pts)
  v_model <- fit.variogram(v_emp, vgm(psill = var(fit_df$target), model = variogramModel, range = max(v_emp$dist) / 3, nugget = var(fit_df$target) / 4))

  filled <- df$target
  if (nrow(pred_df) > 0) {
    pred_pts <- pred_df
    coordinates(pred_pts) <- ~x + y
    k <- krige(target ~ 1, fit_pts, pred_pts, model = v_model, nmax = as.numeric(nmax), debug.level = 0)
    filled[is.na(df$target)] <- as.numeric(k$var1.pred)
  }

} else {

  data_fit <- df[!is.na(df$target) & !is.na(df$covariate), ]
  data_pred <- df[!is.na(df$covariate), ]
  fit_pts <- data_fit
  coordinates(fit_pts) <- ~x + y
  v_emp <- variogram(target ~ 1, fit_pts)
  init_psill <- var(data_fit$target)
  v_cross <- variogram(gstat(gstat(NULL, id = "target", formula = target ~ 1, data = fit_pts), id = "covariate", formula = covariate ~ 1, data = fit_pts))

  # Same multi-start fit as the preview cell above (see its own comment
  # for why a single init_range = max(dist)/3 guess isn't reliable
  # here) -- the downloaded file should reflect whichever fit the
  # reader actually saw on screen, not a cruder one recomputed only
  # for export.
  sse_against_target <- function(model_df) {
    vl <- variogramLine(model_df, dist_vector = v_emp$dist)
    sum((v_emp$gamma - vl$gamma)^2)
  }
  fit_lmc_candidate <- function(init_range) {
    lmc_model <- vgm(psill = init_psill, model = variogramModel, range = init_range, nugget = init_psill / 4)
    fresh_g <- function() gstat(gstat(NULL, id = "target", formula = target ~ 1, data = fit_pts), id = "covariate", formula = covariate ~ 1, data = fit_pts)
    gf <- tryCatch(fit.lmc(v_cross, fresh_g(), model = lmc_model, fit.method = 7, correct.diagonal = 1.01), error = function(e) NULL)
    if (is.null(gf)) gf <- tryCatch(fit.lmc(v_cross, fresh_g(), model = lmc_model, fit.method = 1, correct.diagonal = 1.01), error = function(e) NULL)
    if (is.null(gf)) return(NULL)
    list(g_fit = gf, sse = sse_against_target(gf$model[["target"]]))
  }
  candidates <- Filter(Negate(is.null), lapply(max(v_cross$dist) * c(1 / 6, 1 / 3, 2 / 3, 1), fit_lmc_candidate))
  if (length(candidates) == 0) {
    stop(paste0("Could not fit a coregionalization model between these two bands (often too few co-located pixels, or the bands aren't actually correlated)."))
  }
  g_fit <- candidates[[which.min(sapply(candidates, function(c) c$sse))]]$g_fit

  pred_pts <- data_pred
  coordinates(pred_pts) <- ~x + y
  g_pred <- gstat(NULL, id = "target", formula = target ~ 1, data = fit_pts)
  g_pred <- gstat(g_pred, id = "covariate", formula = covariate ~ 1, data = pred_pts)
  g_pred$model <- g_fit$model
  k <- predict(g_pred, newdata = pred_pts, nmax = as.numeric(nmax), debug.level = 0)

  filled <- df$target
  pred_index <- which(!is.na(df$covariate))
  cokriged <- is.na(df$target[pred_index])
  filled[pred_index[cokriged]] <- as.numeric(k$target.pred[cokriged])

}

filled_band <- rast(matrix(filled, nrow = nrow(r), ncol = ncol(r), byrow = TRUE), extent = ext(r), crs = crs(r))
names(filled_band) <- names(r)[target_i]

out_path <- "/tmp/raster-gap-filler.tif"
writeRaster(filled_band, out_path, overwrite = TRUE, filetype = "GTiff")
raw_bytes <- readBin(out_path, what = "raw", n = file.info(out_path)$size)
jsonlite::base64_enc(raw_bytes)
```

*First run loads the R engine — expect 1-3 minutes (R's WebAssembly
build is noticeably slower to start than this site's Python tools).
Instant after that, and again each time you come back to this page.*

<div id="rgf-dashboard"></div>

<!-- Page-local, not site-wide -- same reasoning as kriging-interpolator.qmd's
     own comment: only tools with a variogram side panel need the ~828KB
     vega bundle. -->
<script src="/vega.min.js"></script>
<script src="/vega-lite.min.js"></script>
<script src="/vega-embed.min.js"></script>
<script src="/vega-chart.js"></script>

<script>
document.addEventListener("DOMContentLoaded", () => {

  const FILL_RAMP = [
    [0.00, 68, 1, 84],
    [0.25, 59, 82, 139],
    [0.50, 33, 144, 140],
    [0.75, 94, 201, 98],
    [1.00, 253, 231, 37]
  ];

  const FOOTPRINT_PAINT = {
    "fill-color": "#42583c",
    "fill-opacity": 0.35,
    "fill-outline-color": "#2a2117"
  };

  const base64ToBytes = (base64Str) => {
    const binary = atob(base64Str);
    const bytes = new Uint8Array(binary.length);
    for (let i = 0; i < binary.length; i++) bytes[i] = binary.charCodeAt(i);
    return bytes;
  };

  const base64ToFloat32 = (base64Str) =>
    new Float32Array(base64ToBytes(base64Str).buffer);

  // nugget + partialSill, both already rounded to 4dp on the R side,
  // can still land on a binary-float artifact when added in JS (e.g.
  // "sill 14.9639999999999999") -- found live on the cross term's own
  // reference-line label. Re-rounding the SUM catches it regardless of
  // which two 4dp numbers produced it.
  const round4 = (n) => Math.round(n * 10000) / 10000;

  // Raw per-band arrays from the inspect cell, keyed by band number --
  // populated once per file (inspect.onResult below), read every time
  // the reader changes Target/Covariate so the preview updates live
  // with no R round trip.
  let rgfBands = null;
  let rgfBounds = null;
  let rgfWidth = 0;
  let rgfHeight = 0;

  // Shows the currently-picked target (+ covariate, if any) BEFORE
  // Fill is pressed -- otherwise the map has nothing to show but the
  // plain footprint rectangle until the reader notices there's a Fill
  // button. Also what redraws the map every time either select
  // changes, and what a completed Fill result gets replaced by again
  // if the reader picks a different pair afterward.
  const renderBandPreview = async () => {

    if (!rgfBands) return;

    const targetSel = document.querySelector("#raster-gap-filler-targetBand");
    const covariateSel = document.querySelector("#raster-gap-filler-covariateBand");
    if (!targetSel || !covariateSel || !targetSel.value) return;

    const dashboard = WebGeoDS.Dashboard.find("raster-gap-filler");
    const target = rgfBands[Number(targetSel.value)];
    if (!target) return;

    const covariateValue = covariateSel.value;
    const covariate = covariateValue && covariateValue !== "None" ? rgfBands[Number(covariateValue)] : null;

    if (covariate) {

      await dashboard.map.setRasterBicolorImage("raster-gap-filler-compute-r", {
        bounds: rgfBounds,
        width: rgfWidth,
        height: rgfHeight,
        channelA: target,
        channelB: covariate
      });

      dashboard.legendWrapEl.replaceChildren(WebGeoDS.legend([
        { color: "rgb(255,0,0)", label: `Target (band ${targetSel.value})` },
        { color: "rgb(0,0,255)", label: `Covariate (band ${covariateValue})` }
      ]));

    } else {

      await dashboard.map.setRasterImage("raster-gap-filler-compute-r", {
        bounds: rgfBounds,
        width: rgfWidth,
        height: rgfHeight,
        values: target.values,
        min: target.min,
        max: target.max,
        colorRamp: FILL_RAMP
      });

      dashboard.legendWrapEl.replaceChildren(WebGeoDS.legend({
        gradient: FILL_RAMP,
        minLabel: `${target.min}`,
        maxLabel: `${target.max}`
      }));

    }

  };

  let rgfChart = null;

  // Vega-Lite's text mark has no built-in background -- these three
  // labels sat as bare text directly on the chart's own gridlines,
  // legible but visually rougher than the article's own d3 chart
  // (kriging-soil-sampling.qmd/cokriging-raster-gap-filling.qmd),
  // which sizes a white pill to each label via a real getBBox()
  // measurement. Same technique here, run once after the chart's own
  // render instead of before: Vega-Lite's rendered <text> elements
  // support getBBox() exactly like d3's do, and this chart (unlike
  // the article's detached-until-measured one) is already attached to
  // the visible DOM by the time this runs, so no attach/detach dance
  // is needed.
  const pillifyReferenceLabels = (container) => {
    const svg = container.querySelector("svg");
    if (!svg) return;
    for (const t of svg.querySelectorAll("text")) {
      if (!/^(nugget|sill|range) /.test(t.textContent || "")) continue;
      const box = t.getBBox();
      const rect = document.createElementNS("http://www.w3.org/2000/svg", "rect");
      rect.setAttribute("x", box.x - 4);
      rect.setAttribute("y", box.y - 2);
      rect.setAttribute("width", box.width + 8);
      rect.setAttribute("height", box.height + 4);
      rect.setAttribute("rx", 3);
      rect.setAttribute("fill", "#fffdf8");
      rect.setAttribute("stroke", "#d8cdb8");
      rect.setAttribute("stroke-width", 1);
      // Vega-Lite's own text marks carry their OWN transform=
      // "translate(x,y)" attribute (unlike the article's plain d3
      // text, positioned via bare x/y with no transform at all) --
      // getBBox() returns coordinates in the space BEFORE that
      // transform applies, so a sibling rect built from those same
      // raw numbers renders in the PARENT's coordinate space instead,
      // landing wherever the text would sit with its translate simply
      // never happening (found live: a rect offset by exactly the
      // transform's own ty from the text it was supposed to sit
      // behind). Copying the same transform onto the rect fixes it.
      const transform = t.getAttribute("transform");
      if (transform) rect.setAttribute("transform", transform);
      t.parentNode.insertBefore(rect, t);
    }
  };

  // Reference-line layers (nugget/sill/range, dashed) shared by both
  // chart shapes below -- pulled out once so the single-panel and
  // per-series-panel builders don't repeat the same six-layer block.
  const referenceLineLayers = (nugget, sill, range, maxDist, domainMin, domainMax) => {
    const rangeNearRightEdge = range > maxDist * 0.75;
    const rangeAlign = rangeNearRightEdge ? "right" : "left";
    const rangeDx = rangeNearRightEdge ? -3 : 3;
    const layers = [
      { "data": { "values": [{}] }, "mark": { "type": "rule", "strokeDash": [4, 3], "color": "#8a8378" },
        "encoding": { "x": { "datum": 0, "type": "quantitative" }, "x2": { "datum": maxDist }, "y": { "datum": nugget, "type": "quantitative" } } },
      { "data": { "values": [{}] }, "mark": { "type": "text", "align": "left", "baseline": "bottom", "dx": 8, "dy": -4, "color": "#8a8378", "fontSize": 11, "fontWeight": 600 },
        "encoding": { "y": { "datum": nugget, "type": "quantitative" }, "x": { "datum": 0, "type": "quantitative" }, "text": { "value": `nugget ${nugget}` } } },
      { "data": { "values": [{}] }, "mark": { "type": "rule", "strokeDash": [4, 3], "color": "#8a8378" },
        "encoding": { "x": { "datum": 0, "type": "quantitative" }, "x2": { "datum": maxDist }, "y": { "datum": sill, "type": "quantitative" } } },
      { "data": { "values": [{}] }, "mark": { "type": "text", "align": "right", "baseline": "bottom", "dx": -2, "dy": -2, "color": "#8a8378", "fontSize": 11, "fontWeight": 600 },
        "encoding": { "y": { "datum": sill, "type": "quantitative" }, "x": { "datum": maxDist, "type": "quantitative" }, "text": { "value": `sill ${sill}` } } },
      { "data": { "values": [{}] }, "mark": { "type": "rule", "strokeDash": [4, 3], "color": "#8a8378" },
        "encoding": { "x": { "datum": range, "type": "quantitative" }, "y": { "datum": domainMin, "type": "quantitative" }, "y2": { "datum": domainMax } } },
      // baseline "bottom" + a small NEGATIVE dy, not "top"/+3 -- found
      // live that placing this label just below domainMin (the plot's
      // own bottom edge) put it in the same band Vega-Lite draws its
      // own x-axis tick numbers in, overlapping them. Lifting it a few
      // px back inside the plot area (the same "just above the axis
      // line" spot the article's own d3 pillLabel() uses for this
      // exact label) clears them.
      { "data": { "values": [{}] }, "mark": { "type": "text", "align": rangeAlign, "baseline": "bottom", "dx": rangeDx, "dy": -3, "color": "#8a8378", "fontSize": 11, "fontWeight": 600 },
        "encoding": { "x": { "datum": range, "type": "quantitative" }, "y": { "datum": domainMin, "type": "quantitative" }, "text": { "value": `range ${range}px` } } }
    ];
    // The domain floor only actually sits below 0 for a cross term
    // (a legitimate negative covariance) -- target/covariate's own
    // nugget is never negative, so this rule would just retrace the
    // x-axis there and is skipped.
    if (domainMin < -1e-9) {
      layers.unshift({
        "data": { "values": [{}] },
        "mark": { "type": "rule", "strokeDash": [2, 2], "color": "#8a8378" },
        "encoding": { "x": { "datum": 0, "type": "quantitative" }, "x2": { "datum": maxDist }, "y": { "datum": 0, "type": "quantitative" } }
      });
    }
    return layers;
  };

  // One chart, two shapes: no covariate means only the target's own
  // variogram exists (v.variogram.covariate absent) and this draws a
  // single empirical+fitted+reference-line chart, the same shape
  // kriging-interpolator.qmd's own side panel already uses. A
  // covariate means fit.lmc() ALSO produced the covariate's own
  // variogram and the cross-variogram between the two -- already
  // computed inside the compute cell for the fit itself, just never
  // read back out before now -- shown as three STACKED panels rather
  // than overlaid: found live (screenshot review) that overlaying them
  // on one shared scale made it impossible to tell a genuinely close
  // fit from a poor one, since the three series rarely share a
  // sensible common y-range. Each panel gets its own scale and its own
  // nugget/sill/range reference lines instead. Colors echo this tool's
  // own bicolor map preview above (red family = target, blue family =
  // covariate) plus purple/magenta for the cross term, the same hue
  // family that preview shows where the two overlap -- softened from
  // that preview's own pure red/blue so the chart's points and lines
  // stay readable against the page's cream background instead of
  // reading as neon.
  const renderVariogramChart = async (dashboard, v) => {

    rgfChart?.destroy();
    rgfChart = null;

    if (!v || !v.variogram) return;

    const isComposite = !!v.variogram.covariate;
    const range = v.summary.range;

    const seriesDefs = isComposite
      ? [
          { key: "target", label: `Target (band ${v.summary.targetBand})`, color: "#e60000", data: v.variogram.target },
          { key: "covariate", label: `Covariate (band ${v.summary.covariateBand})`, color: "#0000e6", data: v.variogram.covariate },
          { key: "cross", label: "Cross (target × covariate)", color: "#a000a0", data: v.variogram.cross }
        ]
      : [
          { key: "target", label: `Target (band ${v.summary.targetBand})`, color: "#ab502b", data: v.variogram.target }
        ];

    let maxDist = range;
    for (const s of seriesDefs) {
      for (const arr of [s.data.empirical, s.data.fitted]) {
        for (const d of arr.dist) { if (d > maxDist) maxDist = d; }
      }
    }
    const xDomain = [0, maxDist * 1.05];

    const chartWidth = Math.max(200, (dashboard.sidePanelEl.getBoundingClientRect().width || 300) - 50);

    if (!isComposite) {

      const s = seriesDefs[0];
      const nugget = s.data.nugget;
      const sill = round4(s.data.nugget + s.data.partialSill);
      let minGamma = Math.min(0, nugget), maxGamma = Math.max(0, sill);
      for (const arr of [s.data.empirical, s.data.fitted]) {
        for (const g of arr.gamma) { if (g < minGamma) minGamma = g; if (g > maxGamma) maxGamma = g; }
      }
      const domainMin = minGamma * 1.05, domainMax = maxGamma * 1.05;
      const empRows = s.data.empirical.dist.map((d, i) => ({ dist: d, gamma: s.data.empirical.gamma[i], npairs: s.data.empirical.npairs[i], key: `emp-${i}` }));
      const fitRows = s.data.fitted.dist.map((d, i) => ({ dist: d, gamma: s.data.fitted.gamma[i], key: `fit-${i}` }));

      rgfChart = await WebGeoDS.renderVegaChart(dashboard.sidePanelEl, {
        "$schema": "https://vega.github.io/schema/vega-lite/v5.json",
        "title": "Empirical variogram and fitted model",
        "width": chartWidth,
        "height": 220,
        "autosize": { "type": "pad" },
        "params": [{ "name": "rgfExternal", "value": null }],
        "layer": [
          {
            "data": { "values": empRows },
            "params": [{ "name": "rgfSelect_target", "select": { "type": "point", "fields": ["key"] } }],
            "mark": { "type": "point", "filled": true, "size": 70, "color": s.color },
            "encoding": {
              "x": { "field": "dist", "type": "quantitative", "title": "Distance (px)", "scale": { "domain": xDomain } },
              "y": { "field": "gamma", "type": "quantitative", "title": "Semivariance", "scale": { "domain": [domainMin, domainMax] } },
              "tooltip": [{ "field": "dist", "title": "Distance (px)" }, { "field": "gamma", "title": "Semivariance" }, { "field": "npairs", "title": "Point pairs" }]
            }
          },
          { "data": { "values": fitRows }, "mark": { "type": "line", "color": "#ab502b" },
            "encoding": { "x": { "field": "dist", "type": "quantitative" }, "y": { "field": "gamma", "type": "quantitative" } } },
          ...referenceLineLayers(nugget, sill, range, maxDist, domainMin, domainMax)
        ]
      }, {
        selectParams: ["rgfSelect_target"],
        externalParam: "rgfExternal",
        keyField: "key",
        onSelect: () => {}
      });

      pillifyReferenceLabels(dashboard.sidePanelEl);

      return;

    }

    // Composite case: one vconcat panel per series, same multi-view
    // shape spatial-classifier.qmd's own side panel already
    // establishes (a top-level shared externalParam, each panel
    // declaring its own point-selection param).
    const buildPanel = (s) => {

      const nugget = s.data.nugget;
      const sill = round4(s.data.nugget + s.data.partialSill);
      let minGamma = Math.min(0, nugget), maxGamma = Math.max(0, sill);
      for (const arr of [s.data.empirical, s.data.fitted]) {
        for (const g of arr.gamma) { if (g < minGamma) minGamma = g; if (g > maxGamma) maxGamma = g; }
      }
      const domainMin = minGamma * 1.05, domainMax = maxGamma * 1.05;
      const empRows = s.data.empirical.dist.map((d, i) => ({ dist: d, gamma: s.data.empirical.gamma[i], npairs: s.data.empirical.npairs[i], key: `${s.key}-emp-${i}` }));
      const fitRows = s.data.fitted.dist.map((d, i) => ({ dist: d, gamma: s.data.fitted.gamma[i], key: `${s.key}-fit-${i}` }));

      return {
        "title": s.label,
        "width": "container",
        "height": 140,
        "layer": [
          {
            "data": { "values": empRows },
            "params": [{ "name": `rgfSelect_${s.key}`, "select": { "type": "point", "fields": ["key"] } }],
            "mark": { "type": "point", "filled": true, "size": 45, "color": s.color },
            "encoding": {
              "x": { "field": "dist", "type": "quantitative", "title": "Distance (px)", "scale": { "domain": xDomain } },
              "y": { "field": "gamma", "type": "quantitative", "title": "Semivariance", "scale": { "domain": [domainMin, domainMax] } },
              "tooltip": [{ "field": "dist", "title": "Distance (px)" }, { "field": "gamma", "title": "Value" }, { "field": "npairs", "title": "Point pairs" }]
            }
          },
          { "data": { "values": fitRows }, "mark": { "type": "line", "color": s.color },
            "encoding": { "x": { "field": "dist", "type": "quantitative" }, "y": { "field": "gamma", "type": "quantitative" } } },
          ...referenceLineLayers(nugget, sill, range, maxDist, domainMin, domainMax)
        ]
      };

    };

    rgfChart = await WebGeoDS.renderVegaChart(dashboard.sidePanelEl, {
      "$schema": "https://vega.github.io/schema/vega-lite/v5.json",
      // "fit-x" (not "pad", the single-panel chart's own choice above)
      // -- found live with spatial-classifier.qmd's own vconcat side
      // panel that "pad" leaves Vega-Lite's default autosize in
      // charge for a concatenated spec, which computes a width wider
      // than sidePanelEl's real box and gets silently clipped by its
      // own overflow:hidden instead of erroring.
      "autosize": { "type": "fit-x", "contains": "padding" },
      "params": [{ "name": "rgfExternal", "value": null }],
      "vconcat": seriesDefs.map(buildPanel)
    }, {
      selectParams: seriesDefs.map((s) => `rgfSelect_${s.key}`),
      externalParam: "rgfExternal",
      keyField: "key",
      onSelect: () => {}
    });

    pillifyReferenceLabels(dashboard.sidePanelEl);

  };

  new WebGeoDS.Dashboard({
    tool: "raster-gap-filler",
    mount: "#rgf-dashboard",
    layout: { sidePanel: { id: "rgf-chart", flex: "1 1 280px", minWidth: "260px" } },
    upload: { languages: ["r"], kind: "raster", label: "📁 Upload" },
    example: {
      cellId: "raster-gap-filler-example-r",
      kind: "raster",
      status: "✓ example 2-band raster loaded — pick a target and (optionally) a covariate band, then Fill."
    },
    emptyStats: [
      ["Dimensions", "—"],
      ["—", "Upload a multi-band .tif/.tiff file or load the example above"]
    ],
    inspect: {
      cellId: "raster-gap-filler-inspect-r",
      layers: [
        { source: "raster-gap-filler-inspect-r", from: (v) => v.footprint, type: "fill", paint: () => FOOTPRINT_PAINT, fit: true }
      ],
      stats: (v) => {
        const s = v.summary;
        if (!s) {
          return [["Dimensions", "—"], ["—", "Upload a multi-band .tif/.tiff file or load the example above"]];
        }
        const bandLines = s.bandStats.map((b) =>
          `Band ${b.band} (${b.name}): ${(b.naFraction * 100).toFixed(0)}% empty`
        );
        return [
          ["Dimensions", `${s.width} × ${s.height} px`],
          ["Bands", String(s.bandCount)],
          ["CRS", s.crs],
          ["Per-band gaps", bandLines.join(" · ")]
        ];
      },
      // Stashes every band's raw values so renderBandPreview() (below
      // the Dashboard constructor) can draw the target/covariate
      // preview without asking R to recompute anything -- then draws
      // it once immediately with whichever pair _syncSelectInputs()
      // (shared/dashboard.js, runs just before this onResult) already
      // defaulted to.
      onResult: async (v) => {

        if (!v || !v.summary || !v.bands) {
          rgfBands = null;
          await WebGeoDS.Dashboard.find("raster-gap-filler").map.removeRasterImage("raster-gap-filler-compute-r");
          return;
        }

        rgfBands = {};
        for (const b of v.bands) {
          rgfBands[b.band] = { values: base64ToFloat32(b.data), min: b.min, max: b.max };
        }
        rgfBounds = v.summary.wgs84Bounds;
        rgfWidth = v.summary.width;
        rgfHeight = v.summary.height;

        await renderBandPreview();

      }
    },
    compute: {
      cellId: "raster-gap-filler-compute-r",
      label: "▶ Fill",
      busyLabel: "⌛ Kriging...",
      inputs: [
        { kind: "select", name: "targetBand", label: "Target:",
          options: (v) => Array.from({ length: v.summary?.bandCount ?? 0 }, (_, i) => String(i + 1)),
          default: (v) => String(v.summary?.suggestedTarget ?? 1) },
        { kind: "select", name: "covariateBand", label: "Covariate:",
          options: (v) => ["None", ...Array.from({ length: v.summary?.bandCount ?? 0 }, (_, i) => String(i + 1))],
          default: (v) => {
            const n = v.summary?.bandCount ?? 0;
            const target = v.summary?.suggestedTarget ?? 1;
            if (n < 2) return "None";
            const other = Array.from({ length: n }, (_, i) => i + 1).find((b) => b !== target);
            return other ? String(other) : "None";
          } },
        { kind: "select", name: "variogramModel", label: "Model:",
          options: () => ["Sph", "Exp", "Gau"],
          default: () => "Sph" },
        { kind: "slider", name: "nmax", label: "Neighbourhood size", range: [10, 60], value: 24, step: 2 }
      ],
      legend: (v) => ({
        gradient: FILL_RAMP,
        minLabel: `${v.raster.min}`,
        maxLabel: `${v.raster.max}`
      }),
      stats: (v) => {
        const s = v.summary;
        const rows = [
          ["Target band", String(s.targetBand)],
          ["Covariate band", s.covariateBand ? String(s.covariateBand) : "None (ordinary kriging)"],
          ["Variogram model", s.variogramModel],
          ["Nugget", s.nugget],
          ["Partial sill", s.partialSill],
          ["Range (px)", s.range],
          // The target's own known-pixel mean/variance -- not from the
          // fitted model, so they double as a sanity check: nugget +
          // partial sill landing far from this variance is the
          // clearest sign the fit is off, without this card asserting
          // a verdict of its own (a hardcoded threshold would flag
          // genuinely non-stationary data as often as an actual bad
          // fit, so the two numbers are left side by side for the
          // reader to compare rather than pre-judged here).
          ["Sample mean", s.sampleMean],
          ["Sample variance", s.sampleVariance],
          ["Neighbourhood size", String(s.nmax)],
          ["Pixels filled", s.pixelsFilled.toLocaleString()]
        ];
        if (s.crossValidationRmse !== null && s.crossValidationRmse !== undefined) {
          rows.push(["Cross-validation RMSE", s.crossValidationRmse]);
        }
        if (s.pixelsStillEmpty > 0) {
          rows.push(["Still empty", `${s.pixelsStillEmpty.toLocaleString()} (no covariate data there either)`]);
        }
        if (s.fitMethodFallback) {
          rows.push(["⚠️ Fit method", "fell back to a cruder weighting (Cressie's own fit failed on this data)"]);
        }
        return rows;
      },
      onResult: async (v) => {

        const dashboard =
          WebGeoDS.Dashboard.find("raster-gap-filler");

        if (!v) {
          await dashboard.map.removeRasterImage("raster-gap-filler-compute-r");
          await renderVariogramChart(dashboard, null);
          return;
        }

        await dashboard.map.setRasterImage("raster-gap-filler-compute-r", {
          bounds: v.raster.wgs84Bounds,
          width: v.raster.width,
          height: v.raster.height,
          values: new Float32Array(base64ToBytes(v.raster.data).buffer),
          min: v.raster.min,
          max: v.raster.max,
          colorRamp: FILL_RAMP
        });

        await renderVariogramChart(dashboard, v);

      },
      download: {
        raster: {
          label: "⬇ Download GeoTIFF",
          prepare: (value, inputs) => {
            if (!value) return false;
            window.targetBand = inputs.targetBand;
            window.covariateBand = inputs.covariateBand;
            window.variogramModel = inputs.variogramModel;
            window.nmax = inputs.nmax;
          },
          cellId: "raster-gap-filler-export-r",
          decode: base64ToBytes,
          getFilename: () => "gap-filled.tif"
        }
      }
    }
  });

  // Hand-wired, same as raster-inspector.qmd's own Band-menu listener
  // -- Dashboard only reads these two selects at Fill time
  // (runCompute()'s _readInputs()), so redrawing the live preview on
  // every change is this tool's own responsibility, not something a
  // declarative `inputs` entry triggers by itself.
  document.querySelector("#raster-gap-filler-targetBand")?.addEventListener("change", renderBandPreview);
  document.querySelector("#raster-gap-filler-covariateBand")?.addEventListener("change", renderBandPreview);

});
</script>

<style>
#raster-gap-filler-example-r, #raster-gap-filler-inspect-r, #raster-gap-filler-compute-r, #raster-gap-filler-export-r {
  height: 0;
  overflow: hidden;
  margin: 0;
  padding: 0;
  border: 0;
}
</style>

<div class="webgeods-closing-note">
Got sparse point samples instead of a raster with gaps? The
<a href="/tools/kriging-interpolator.html">Kriging Interpolator</a>
predicts a full surface from scattered measurements. Want to look at a
raster's bands before deciding what to fill? Start with the
<a href="/tools/raster-inspector.html">Raster Inspector</a>.
</div>
